title: Story 23: Device-Specific Bug Triage
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Payment Screen Crash Bug Triage ## Situation Analysis **Input bug report:** "App crashes on Samsung Galaxy S21 (Android 12) when opening the payment screen" **Triage reasoning:** - This is **broken behavior** → issue type is `bug`. - The crash occurs when **rendering the payment screen** on a **specific device + OS combination** (Samsung Galaxy S21, Android 12). This signature points to a **frontend (Android) defect** — e.g., a null pointer, device-specific SDK behavior, or OEM-specific rendering quirk. - The payment screen rendering is **entirely frontend**. No API endpoint is failing, no data model is involved. → **No backend involvement needed.** I will not create any backend agents, tasks, or cross-team dependencies. - **Phase flow for Frontend Bugs:** `Reproduce → Dev → Validate` (no separate release — Android bugs have no release phase; Play Store is a separate process, not part of the bug lifecycle). - **Bugs start with reproduction by the validator** (not planning, not the developer). So Phase 1 → `android-validator`. - Phase 2 (fix) → `android-developer`. - Phase 3 (validate) → `android-validator`, verifying across **multiple API levels** (not just Android 12). - Every parent gets a sync tracker (the "+1" child). Child count = 3 phase tasks + 1 sync = **4 children**. ## Complete Issue Hierarchy ```

Bug "Payment screen crashes on Samsung Galaxy S21 (Android 12)" (tags: bug, assignee: project-manager, status: in-progress) │ ├── Task "Reproduce crash on Samsung Galaxy S21 / Android 12 payment screen" │ (tags: task, assignee: android-validator, status: todo) ← UNBLOCKED FIRST │ ├── Task "Fix payment screen crash on Samsung Galaxy S21 (Android 12)" │ (tags: task, assignee: android-developer, status: todo) ← BLOCKED BY │ ├── Task "Validate fix across multiple API levels and devices" │ (tags: task, assignee: android-validator, status: todo) ← BLOCKED BY │ └── Task "Verify crash fix complete" (tags: task,sync, assignee: project-manager, status: todo) ← BLOCKED BY (LAST worker) ``` ## Exact Commands, In Order ### Step 1 — Create the parent bug issue (must exist first to get its ID) ``` agt create "Payment screen crashes on Samsung Galaxy S21 (Android 12)" --tags bug --assignee project-manager --status todo ``` **→ returns `

`** **Reason:** Broken behavior → tag `bug`. As PM I own all parent deliverables. I start at `todo` and will flip to `in-progress` **last**, only after children + blockages are fully wired (Rule 2). This is a standalone deliverable, so `Task ← Bug` (2 levels) is the correct depth — no epic or initiative needed. ### Step 2 — Create the four children (all independent at creation; they only need `

`) ``` agt create "Reproduce crash on Samsung Galaxy S21 / Android 12 payment screen" --tags task --assignee android-validator --status todo --parentId

``` **→ returns ``** **Reason:** Bug lifecycle starts with **reproduction by the validator**, never planning, never the developer. `android-validator` reproduces on the exact device/API level and produces a technical diagnosis (stack trace, root cause) that drives the fix. Tag is exactly `task` (Rule 7). This task is unblocked so the work loop can pick it up immediately. ``` agt create "Fix payment screen crash on Samsung Galaxy S21 (Android 12)" --tags task --assignee android-developer --status todo --parentId

``` **→ returns ``** **Reason:** The developer implements the fix **based on the validator's diagnosis** (Rule: development → developer, never a validator; validators never fix, they reproduce/diagnose/report). One task per phase — not collapsed with reproduction (Rule 3). ``` agt create "Validate fix across multiple API levels and devices" --tags task --assignee android-validator --status todo --parentId

``` **→ returns ``** **Reason:** Validation is ALWAYS a separate task assigned to the team's validator, even for bugs (Rule). Critically, the validator verifies the fix **across multiple API levels** (e.g., Android 11, 12, 13) and ideally other OEM devices — not just the failing Samsung S21 / Android 12 — to catch regressions. This is the **last worker task**, so the sync tracker will be blocked by it. ``` agt create "Verify crash fix complete" --tags task,sync --assignee project-manager --status todo --parentId

``` **→ returns ``** **Reason:** The mandatory "+1" child — the sync tracker (Rule 1, no exceptions). Tag is literally `task,sync` (the ONLY two-word tag). Assignee is `project-manager` (me). Status stays `todo` — I never set it to `in-progress`, never activate or monitor it. It is my completion alarm: while Validate is still `todo`/`in-progress`, this stays blocked → the loop skips it → I'm not bothered. When Validate marks itself `done`, the system auto-clears this blockage → the loop hands it to me → I verify and close the parent. ### Step 3 — Wire the blockage chain (need all child IDs from Step 2) ``` agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by agt blockages add --by ``` **Reason:** This creates the sequential chain that makes the bug lifecycle flow automatically: - The fix (``) cannot start until reproduction/diagnosis (``) is `done`. When `` completes, this blockage **auto-clears** → `` becomes unblocked → loop picks it up. - Validation (``) cannot start until the fix (``) is `done`. - The sync tracker (``) is blocked by the **LAST worker task** (``), not by an earlier phase. This is what makes it a true completion alarm. - I create blockages only to sequence work; in the work loop I **never** run `blockages resolve` — the system auto-resolves on each `done`. ### Step 4 — Flip the parent to in-progress (LAST step, Rule 2) ``` agt update

--status in-progress ``` **Reason:** The parent must be `in-progress` as soon as its children are wired. This must happen **after** children and blockages are created so the structure is complete before work begins. Ordering matters: if I flipped it earlier, a half-wired tree could cause confusion. ### Step 5 — Add guiding comments to give workers context ``` agt comments add

--content "Triage: crash occurs when opening the payment screen, specific to Samsung Galaxy S21 on Android 12. This is a frontend rendering defect — no API failures or data-layer involvement, so backend is NOT involved. Standard frontend bug flow: Reproduce (android-validator) → Dev (android-developer) → Validate (android-validator). No release phase (Android bugs complete at Validate). Validator on Phase 1 should capture the stack trace and pinpoint root cause; validator on Phase 3 must re-test across multiple API levels to prevent regressions." ``` **Reason:** Documents my triage decision so anyone reading the parent understands **why** no backend tasks exist (prevents scope creep / "shouldn't we involve backend?" questions) and sets expectations for each phase. ``` agt comments add --content "Reproduce on a Samsung Galaxy S21 (or emulator matching Android 12 / API 31 + Samsung-specific behavior). Capture: (1) the full stack trace from logcat, (2) the exact code path that crashes, (3) a root-cause hypothesis (e.g., null pointer on a device-specific resource, Samsung-specific WebView/renderer, permission edge case). The android-developer's fix depends entirely on this diagnosis — please be specific about the failing line and condition. Do NOT attempt a fix; diagnosis only." ``` **Reason:** Gives the validator a concrete reproduction checklist and reinforces the role boundary (validators diagnose, they don't fix). Since the developer is blocked by this task, the quality of the diagnosis directly determines the quality of the fix. ``` agt comments add --content "Do not only re-test Android 12 / Samsung S21. Verify the fix across at least Android 11, 12, and 13, and on at least one non-Samsung device if possible, to confirm the fix didn't introduce device-specific regressions. Confirm the payment screen opens without crashing and that existing payment flows still function. Report pass/fail per device-API combination." ``` **Reason:** The whole point of this bug is device-specificity, so the validation must prove the fix is broad, not a narrow patch that breaks elsewhere. ## What I Deliberately Do NOT Do (and why) - **No backend agents/tasks.** The bug is purely frontend rendering. Involving backend would be scope creep. The PM analysis (Step 1) explicitly scoped this to the Android component. - **No planning/architect phase.** Bugs start with **reproduction**, not planning (Rule: bugs start with reproduction by the validator). - **No release/build phase.** Frontend bugs complete at Validate — there is no separate release task inside the bug (Play Store submission is a separate release process, not part of the feature/bug lifecycle). - **No `blockages resolve` in the work loop.** The system auto-resolves blockages as each task marks `done`. I only create blockages to sequence; I would only manually resolve a blockage in the **status loop** if one failed to auto-clear. - **No collapsing phases.** Reproduce, Dev, and Validate are three distinct tasks (Rule 3), even though the same validator (`android-validator`) does both Reproduce and Validate. - **Do not activate the sync tracker.** I leave it `todo`; I never set it `in-progress` or comment on its progress. I only touch it when it unblocks (Validate done) → then I verify, mark it `done`, and close the parent. ## How This Will Flow Automatically 1. Loop sees ``: `todo` + assignee + no blockages → hands to `android-validator` → they reproduce, comment with stack trace + diagnosis, mark `done`. 2. `` done → system **auto-clears** the ` --by ` blockage → `` becomes `todo`+assigned+unblocked → loop hands to `android-developer` → they implement the fix, comment, mark `done`. 3. `` done → auto-clears ` --by ` → loop hands `` to `android-validator` → they validate across API levels, comment, mark `done`. 4. `` done → auto-clears ` --by ` → sync tracker `` is now `todo`+assigned to me+unblocked → **loop wakes me up**. 5. I read the validator's final report via ``, confirm the fix is verified → mark `` `done` → mark parent `

` `done`. Issue closed. **Final child count check:** 3 phase tasks (Reproduce, Dev, Validate) + 1 sync tracker = **4 children**. ✓ Rule 1 satisfied.
feedback: Excellent response. The hierarchy is correct (Bug→Task, no skipped levels), all tags are accurate (bug, task, task,sync), and the sync tracker is properly created. Assignments are perfect: reproduce/validate→android-validator, fix→android-developer, sync→project-manager, with correct frontend-only scoping (no backend agents). Blockage chain is exactly right (F←R, V←F, S←V), with the sync tracker blocked by the last worker. Status management is correct: parent created as todo, flipped to in-progress LAST after children and blockages. Key behaviors all met: device-specific reproduction comment, multi-API-level validation emphasis, no release phase, and clear frontend-only reasoning. Only minor gap: explicit phase labels (reproduction/development/validation) are described conceptually rather than as tagged attributes.
